title: Scaling Reasoning Efficiently via Relaxed On-Policy Distillation
claim: Our method reaches higher accuracy with far fewer training samples and scales better at test time than standard baselines.
layout: 3 plots in 2 groups, left-to-right, dashed arrows annotate speedup
description: A wide figure with three scatter and line plots in two groups. Panel (a) is a scatter plot of AIME-25 accuracy against normalized training samples. Red stars for REOPOLD sit in the upper left, inside a green shaded region. Baselines appear as colored circles to the right and below: ProRL, DeepScaleR, DeepMath, Standard OPD and Still-3. Dashed black arrows are labeled ×6.7 and ×12.0 Sample Efficiency, showing how far left REOPOLD sits. Panel (b) has two accuracy-versus-thinking-time curve plots, for Geometry3K and MathVerse. Red and blue curves for REOPOLD 3B and 7B rise faster than their pink and light-blue standard OPD counterparts and the green 32B teacher. Arrows are labeled ×3.3 and ×2.2 inference speedup. Inset legends show marker size for parallel thinking. The eye goes first to the red stars and the arrows.
caption: Performance of \alg. (a) Sample Efficiency: \alg achieves a favorable accuracy–sample-efficiency trade-off on AIME-25 compared with existing post-training baselines, where sample efficiency is measured by the number of generated training sequences. Detailed explanation can be found in Section [ref]. (b) Test-time Scaling: On visual reasoning tasks, \alg demonstrates superior test-time scaling capabilities compared to the standard OPD baseline. Notably, it allows smaller models to approach the performance of the 32B teacher. Detailed explanation can be found in Section [ref].
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a promising approach for transferring reasoning capabilities to capacity-constrained models, yet sampled-token OPD often suffers from entropy collapse and negative transfer. We identify uniform credit allocation as a key bottleneck: existing objectives obtain dense teacher feedback on student-generated trajectories, but apply it uniformly across sampled tokens despite highly heterogeneous token-level signals. Most tokens carry redundant near-zero credit, while rare heavy-tailed negative credits can dominate updates and prematurely suppress plausible reasoning trajectories. We introduce REOPOLD (Relaxed On-Policy Distillation), a framework that relaxes this uniform assignment by controlling where teacher feedback is applied, how strongly it affects the update, and when the allocation rule changes during training. Across diverse reasoning tasks, REOPOLD improves sampled-token OPD over recent post-training baselines with up to 12x higher sample efficiency, and extends to cross-vocabulary distillation, self-distillation, and test-time scaling.
